questions.text: "___ being controversial, the film attracted enormous audiences." (concession)
"The novel is brilliantly written. ___, it is difficult to follow." (contrast — new sentence)
questions.hint: "However" at the start of a new sentence introduces a contrast

questions.text: "___ its unusual structure, the novel initially failed to find a publisher." (cause)
questions.correct: Owing to / Due to / Because of

questions.text: "The director uses extreme long shots ___ emphasise the characters' isolation." (purpose)
"The film's ambiguous ending divided audiences. ___, it sparked significant critical debate." (effect)
"___ the film has structural weaknesses, it succeeds emotionally." (concession clause)
questions.hint: "Although + subject + verb" = concession with a full clause

questions.text: "The acting is superb. ___, the cinematography is extraordinary." (addition)
"The novel explores grief. ___, it offers a meditation on identity and belonging." (addition of equal weight)
"The film was banned. ___, its readership grew internationally." (unexpected positive despite negative)
questions.hint: "Nevertheless" = despite a negative situation, a positive occurred

questions.text: "___, this film represents a significant achievement in world cinema, despite its imperfections." (conclusion)
questions.correct: Overall / In conclusion / Ultimately / On balance
questions.hint: Summary linker for a concluding judgement

questions.text: According to Reading 1, what does neuroscience research show about reading fiction?
opts: It activates regions associated with emotion, social cognition, and physical experience
It has no measurable effect on the brain
It reduces empathy in some readers
questions.correct: It activates regions associated with emotion, social cognition, and physical experience

questions.text: "The score was criticised, ___ the cast's performances were universally praised."
"___, I examined structure. ___, I will analyse language choices." (sequence)
"___ the novel's commercial failure, it won the Booker Prize."
questions.hint: "Despite + noun" = concession (acknowledging the failure while noting the prize)

questions.text: What does Ruslan say about great art?
opts: It should always have a clear moral message
It is defined by what it leaves out, not just what it includes
questions.correct: It is defined by what it leaves out, not just what it includes

questions.text: Which is the most precise way to show artistic intention?
opts: The director used silence so we feel uncomfortable.
The director used silence. Consequently, we feel uncomfortable.
The director uses silence in order to create discomfort and resist easy emotional interpretation.
The director used silence because it was better.
questions.correct: The director uses silence in order to create discomfort and resist easy emotional interpretation.
questions.hint: "In order to + infinitive" = most precise expression of purpose

questions.text: "The film ___ explores trauma ___ examines how memory shapes identity." (equal emphasis on both aspects)
questions.hint: "Not only… but also" = equal emphasis on two elements

questions.text: What does Prof. Dzhaksybekov say good criticism asks?
opts: What is it attempting to do, by what means, and why does it matter?
Who made the work and when?
questions.correct: What is it attempting to do, by what means, and why does it matter?
questions.hint: Listening 3B: Prof. Dzhaksybekov's definition of criticism

questions.text: "Despite ___ the film was slow, I found it compelling." — What is wrong?
opts: "Despite" should be "although" — despite cannot precede a full clause
questions.correct: "Despite" should be "although" — despite cannot precede a full clause

questions.text: "___ balance, the film succeeds on its own terms despite occasional weaknesses." (final judgement)
questions.hint: "On balance" = weighing all sides before a final verdict

questions.text: "The novel is long and dense. ___, it is also deeply rewarding." (contrast — unexpected positive)
"Productive uncertainty about what a text means" is called literary ___.
"___ its ambiguous ending, the film attracted a wide audience." (cause)
"The novel is brilliant; however, it has flaws" is correctly punctuated.
questions.hint: Semicolon + however + comma = correct punctuation for "however"

questions.text: "Intertextuality" in literary analysis means…
opts: The relationships between texts — one responding to or building on another
questions.correct: The relationships between texts — one responding to or building on another
questions.hint: Reading 2: "texts are in conversation with earlier texts"
